reference_implementation.rule: the campaign refuses to score (REFUSED_REFERENCE_CHANGED) if any reference file sha256 in the scoring tree differs from sha256_at_registration; a changed reference requires a new contract version
reference_implementation.invocation: the harness imports the scoring tree's unmodified abep_sim modules in-process (python3 -B, cwd = the scoring tree) and executes each registered step with the arguments of the case language below; an exception is captured as the step's refusal identity

environment.blas: scipy-openblas 0.3.31.188.0 (numpy show_config); the reference arithmetic here is RegularGridInterpolator's linear evaluation (no BLAS call)

functions_or_entry_points: abep_hall::registry::{validate_record, read_records, verify, lookup_map_meta, build_registration, register, withdraw, canonical_json_sha256, sha256_canonical_jsonl}
binary `abep-hall-cases` (crates/abep-hall/src/bin/): executes one registered step (JSON on stdin) and prints its outcome
rust_implementation.rust_commit: FILL at scoring time (recorded in the report build_provenance, not here)
design_constraints: JSON documents are read with Python json semantics through abep_provenance::verifier::PyValue (object order = file order, a duplicate key keeps its first position and its last value, int / float / bool distinct)
Python value semantics where the reference depends on them: ==, `in` on str / list / dict, truthiness, hashability (TypeError for list / dict ids), str() / repr() in messages, sorted() of strings

numpy float-array conversion of axes and fields: numbers, booleans (0 / 1) and null (NaN); regular nested lists in C order; ragged nesting, non-numeric strings and objects are refused with the numpy error class

multilinear query reproduces scipy 1.17.1 RegularGridInterpolator(method='linear', bounds_error=True) operation for operation: _check_points (strictly ascending or descending, descending axes flipped), find_indices / find_interval_ascending (single-point axes index -1), the Cython evaluate_linear_2d fast path for two axes and the generic hypercube _evaluate_linear otherwise (same summation and multiplication order), _prepare_xi bounds check
the trust cube uses numpy.searchsorted(side='left') - 1 clipped to [0, n - 2] (a_max wins when n = 1) exactly as hall_map.py, independently of the interpolation interval
module-authored error messages are reproduced character for character (paths as passed by the caller)

registry records are written as json.dumps(rec, sort_keys=True, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + newline, created exclusively (hard link of a fully written, fsynced, read-only temporary file), never overwritten
outputs carry abep_types fail-closed statuses: a refused admission / unadmitted member is NOT_EVALUATED, a query outside the axes OUT_OF_DOMAIN, every other refusal MODEL_ERROR
no Hall physics: the crate interpolates frozen HallThruster.jl maps and gates admission; it computes no discharge quantity
rust_implementation.rule: the report records the sha256 of every provenance source; any later change is UNRECORDED_SOURCE_CHANGE until a scoring execution records it (A9.14 S10.4 RUSTCI-1, generalised)

governing_hashes.rule: both implementations evaluate byte-identical case trees built by the harness and the same repository; the scoring tree's pinned inputs must match pinned_inputs_sha256 (else INPUT_MISMATCH, not a verdict)

frozen_data_read_only: the repository files above are read, never written; case trees are fresh temporary directories, one per case and implementation; INV-03 checks the repository tree is unchanged
no Hall map, ensemble member, decision or registry record of the repository is created, edited or registered

case_language.tree: every case runs in a fresh temporary directory T, built once per implementation from the case's `files` list in order (later entries may overwrite earlier ones); R is the scoring tree (repository root)

file_specs.json: bytes = json.dumps(V).encode() (Python defaults: ensure_ascii, separators ', ' / ': ') after placeholder resolution
file_specs.text: the UTF-8 bytes of the string
file_specs.repo_text_replace: R/<rel> decoded UTF-8, str.replace(old, new, count) (count -1 = all), encoded UTF-8
file_specs.repo_json: json.load(R/<rel>); apply `del` JSON pointers (RFC 6901) in order, then `set` [pointer, value] pairs in order (an existing object key keeps its position, a new one is appended; a list index replaces); json.dumps (defaults)
file_specs.hallmap: a SYNTHETIC map document {meta, axes, fields} (labelled meta.evidence_status = 'SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY_NOT_EVIDENCE', never evidence): meta = {k: 'synthetic' for k in REQUIRED_META} updated with schema 'hall_map_schema_v1', pinned 'commit = "<repository pin>"', ensemble_member_id 'synthetic', ion_wall_losses true, evidence_status, then spec.meta (update) and spec.drop_meta; axes = spec.axes verbatim; fields, in REQUIRED_FIELDS order: spec.fields_raw['@all'] verbatim if given, else a scalar (spec.scalar: flags 1, others 0.02), else a nested list over the axis lengths (top-level len of each axis list) with value 1 for converged / sustained / chemistry_trustworthy / wall_life_trustworthy and, for every other field, spec.fill_scale at the multi-index (nested list, or '@ramp' = 0.5 + i0 + 2 i1 + 4 i2 + 8 i3), default 0.02; spec.flat flattens every field in C order; spec.fields replaces values (position kept); spec.extra_fields are appended; spec.drop_fields removed; spec.drop_top removes top-level keys; spec.replace_meta replaces meta; json.dumps (defaults); spec.text_prefix_axes inserts the given text right after the first '"axes": {' (duplicate-key case)

placeholders.@sha256:<T-relative path>: sha256 of that already-written tree file
placeholders.@gzc:<T-relative path>: sha256 of the decompressed content of that tree file
placeholders.@canon:<T-relative path>#<pointer>: sha256 of json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) of the JSON value at the pointer
placeholders.@abs:T/<rel>: the absolute path of the tree file (per implementation)
placeholders.@step:<k>: the ok value of step k of the same case and implementation (resolved by each implementation's runner)
placeholders.T/<rel>, R/<rel>, T, R: paths in steps, resolved to absolute paths per implementation; null stays null (the module default)

steps.hallmap: m = HallMap(path, bridge_dir, ensemble) with ensemble null (load_ensemble() of R) or json.load(file) (raw, unvalidated override); ok = {names: m.names, shape: [len(m.axes[k]) for k in names], queries: [outcome of m(**q) as a list of [key, value] pairs in dict order]}; a query value given as the string 'nan' / 'inf' / '-inf' is float() of it
steps.load_ensemble: e = load_ensemble(path) (null = the module default R/...); ok = {member_ids: sorted(member_ids(e)), screening_ids: sorted(screening_ids(e))}
steps.require_admitted: require_admitted(member_id, ensemble) with ensemble null, {loaded: path} (load_ensemble(path)) or {raw: path} (json.load); ok = null
steps.register / withdraw / verify / lookup_ma: the hallmap_registry functions with the step's keyword arguments; ensemble null or {raw: path} (json.load, the 'tests only' override); ok = the return value
steps.validate_record: validate_record(record) for a literal record, or for record_from {registry_seq: n} = json.load of the records/ file whose name starts with the zero-padded seq, then `del` / `set` pointers
steps.registry_files: sorted(records/ names) with sha256 of bytes and read-only flag (no write bit), and every '.tmp_' entry left in the registry directory (not compared through a function; written-record EXACT_BYTES evidence)
steps.write / tamper_first_record / remove_fir: tree mutations performed by the harness identically on both trees (tamper: chmod 0644, json.load, set pointers, write json.dumps(rec, sort_keys=True, indent=1) + newline); not compared

randomized_domain.draw: random_map_procedure (seeded from campaign_seeds; numerical parity domain of the multilinear query only)
randomized_domain.domain_note: numerical parity domain only; SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY_NOT_EVIDENCE maps, not a physics, design or evidence claim

random_map_procedure.maps: for i in 0..239, tag t = f'RM|{i}': d = 1 + U(t|dims) % 4 axes named x0..x{d-1}; axis k has n = 1 + U(t|n|k) % 4 points: x[0] = -100 + 200 * u01(t|x0|k), x[j] = x[j-1] + 0.001 + 50 * u01(t|dx|k|j)
random_map_procedure.fields: REQUIRED_FIELDS in order, nested over the axis lengths, flat index p in C order: converged, chemistry_trustworthy, wall_life_trustworthy = 1 if u01(t|f|<name>|p) < 0.85 else 0 (int); sustained = 1 if u < 0.8, 0.9995 if u < 0.9, else 0.5; every other field = (u01(t|f|<name>|p) - 0.5) * 10 ** (U(t|e|<name>|p) % 7 - 3)
random_map_procedure.meta: the hallmap file spec defaults with ion_wall_losses = (u01(t|iwl) < 0.7); the synthetic override ensemble
random_map_procedure.queries: j in 0..5: per axis k, mode = U(t|q|j|k) % 4: 0 -> lo + (hi - lo) * u01(t|v|j|k), 1 -> the node x[U(t|node|j|k) % n], 2 -> lo, 3 -> hi
random_map_procedure.files: written exactly as the hallmap file spec (json.dumps defaults); both implementations read the same bytes

outcome_identity.outcome: each step gives {ok: value} or {err: {kind, message}}; mutation steps give {ok: null} and are not compared
python_kind: KeyError -> KEY_ERROR (message = str(e), the repr of the key)
any other OSError, EOFError, zlib.error -> OS_ERROR
ValueError whose innermost traceback frame filename has a path component 'scipy' (scipy/... or .../scipy/...) -> SCIPY_VALUE_ERROR

ValueError whose message matches a numpy pattern -> NUMPY_VALUE_ERROR:<sub>: RAGGED 'setting an array element with a sequence.*', RESHAPE 'cannot reshape array of size .*', CONVERT 'could not convert string to float: .*', TRUTH 'The truth value of an array .*'
any other ValueError raised from an abep_sim frame -> VALUE_ERROR
outcome_identity.message_not_compared_for: DECODE_ERROR, OS_ERROR, TYPE_ERROR, INDEX_ERROR, NUMPY_VALUE_ERROR:<sub>, OTHER: library-dependent text; the kind (and numpy sub-kind) is compared
outcome_identity.normalisation: before comparison every occurrence of the implementation's own tree root is replaced by '<T>' and of the repository root by '<R>', in messages and in ok values alike
outcome_identity.rust_kind: abep_hall::HallError.kind names exactly one of the kinds above; abep_hall::HallError.status() maps it to the fail-closed vocabulary (NOT_EVALUATED for an unadmitted / screening member, OUT_OF_DOMAIN for a query outside the axes, MODEL_ERROR otherwise)

domain_and_error_parity.cases: every err outcome of the case catalogue (Python side) is a registered DE case; the Rust outcome must have the same kind (and message where compared)
domain_and_error_parity.mapping_rule: every Python exception class / status used by the component maps to exactly one Rust kind; no Rust path may return a value where Python fails, or fail where Python returns, inside the registered domain (CLAUDE.md rule 3: no silent fallbacks)
domain_and_error_parity.registered_domain: the case catalogue and the random maps; JSON documents within RFC 8259 with integers inside 64 bits and nesting depth <= 64

documented_divergence.statement: JSON texts that Python's json accepts beyond RFC 8259 (NaN / Infinity constants, lone surrogate escapes, integers beyond 64 bits, nesting deeper than serde_json's limit) are refused by Rust as DECODE_ERROR
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain; HallThruster.jl (JSON3) and the Python builders never write them; fail closed

documented_divergence.statement: numeric strings inside map axes / fields: numpy converts them with float(); Rust refuses every string element as NUMPY_VALUE_ERROR:CONVERT
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain (maps carry JSON numbers / null); fail closed

documented_divergence.statement: axes nested deeper than two levels: Rust refuses at load (TYPE_ERROR); numpy would build an N-d axis array and fail only at query
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain; fail closed

documented_divergence.statement: the Rust query API takes f64 coordinates; Python float() coercion of str / bool query values has no Rust counterpart
OSError texts other than ENOENT inside registry problem strings (e.g. EACCES) are formatted from the Rust io error and may differ in wording
documented_divergence.disposition: outside the registered domain; the problem is still reported (fail closed)

documented_divergence.statement: a missing or unexpected keyword argument of register / withdraw / build_registration is TYPE_ERROR before any other check in Rust (typed arguments); Python raises TypeError when build_registration is called, after register's non-empty, DRAFT and chain checks
documented_divergence.disposition: every registered case has a single fault, so the outcome is the same; type-level

documented_divergence.statement: the scipy innermost-frame rule of outcome_identity: a ValueError raised in scipy/interpolate/_interpnd.pyx (zero-axis map, case M-23) counts as SCIPY_VALUE_ERROR
documented_divergence.disposition: classification note, not a divergence of behaviour

It is NOT physics validation and it admits no transport member.
